what_its_for: Desmopressin is used to treat bedwetting in children and adults, frequent nighttime urination in adults, diabetes insipidus (a condition where your body makes too much urine), and certain bleeding disorders like mild hemophilia A and von Willebrand disease. It works by mimicking a natural hormone in your body that helps your kidneys hold onto water and reduce urine production.
how_to_take: Desmopressin comes in several forms: a tablet you swallow, a tablet that dissolves under your tongue, a nasal spray, and a nasal solution. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed. For the tablet, swallow it whole with water. For the dissolving tablet, place it under your tongue and let it fully dissolve — do not swallow it whole or drink anything for 5 minutes. For the nasal spray, blow your nose gently first, then spray into your nostril as directed. Do not eat or drink for at least 1 hour before and 8 hours after taking the nasal spray (Noctiva) to lower the risk of low sodium levels. If you are not sure how to use your form of desmopressin, ask your pharmacist to show you.
dosing: Your dose depends on your condition, your age, and the form of desmopressin you are taking. For bedwetting in children and adults, it is usually taken once at bedtime. For nighttime urination in adults, it is taken once at bedtime. For diabetes insipidus, doses may be taken 2 to 3 times a day. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Doses are different for each person, so do not share this medicine with anyone else.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store tablets at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep the nasal spray or solution in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C). Some nasal sprays may be stored at room temperature for a short time — check your product label or ask your pharmacist. Keep all forms of desmopressin out of reach of children. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Limit how much water and other fluids you drink, especially in the evening and at night, unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Drinking too much fluid while taking desmopressin can cause your sodium (salt) levels to drop dangerously low. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase your risk of low sodium. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because some medicines can interact with desmopressin. Avoid activities that require alertness if you feel dizzy or unwell.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: a severe headache, nausea or vomiting, confusion or difficulty thinking clearly, unusual weight gain, swelling of the hands, feet, or face, muscle cramps or weakness, seizures, or feeling very drowsy or faint. These could be signs of low sodium levels, which is a serious side effect. Also contact your doctor if you have chest pain, signs of an allergic reaction (rash, itching, swelling, trouble breathing), or if your condition does not seem to be improving.
when_it_works: For bedwetting and nighttime urination, desmopressin usually starts working within a few hours of your first dose. You may notice fewer wet nights or fewer trips to the bathroom within the first few nights. For diabetes insipidus, you should notice reduced thirst and urination relatively quickly. For bleeding disorders, the medicine works within 15 to 30 minutes of a nasal dose or injection. Full benefit for long-term conditions may take a few weeks. Let your doctor know how well it is working for you.
special_populations: Children: Desmopressin is commonly used for bedwetting in children 6 years and older. Children must have their fluid intake carefully limited in the evening to prevent dangerous drops in sodium. Elderly adults: Older adults are at higher risk of low sodium levels and should be monitored closely. Lower doses are often used. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Desmopressin should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Small amounts may pass into breast milk, so discuss risks with your doctor. Kidney disease: This medicine may not be safe if you have significant kidney problems. Your doctor may not prescribe it or will monitor you very carefully. Heart disease or high blood pressure: Use with caution, as fluid retention can worsen these conditions.
